data.description:
## Description
**What**: Publish plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md (contract_version=1) defining the per-entry schema and the validator acceptance rule, and ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-id-mint.sh that mints stable slug-format intent_ids deterministically.
**Why**: This is the walking-skeleton spine. Every emit/read/validate slice and every downstream consumer (d566, 411b, 7f42, 69e8) references this single contract and intent_id format; without it the rest of the epic has nothing to align to.
**Scope**:
- IN: the contract markdown (per-entry schema: intent_id, owner_ticket, test_artifact{path,kind}, deferred, lightweight, shared_infra, confidence, rationale; manifest-level contract_version=1; unknown-field passthrough requirement; validator acceptance rule); the intent-id-mint.sh helper deriving the slug from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case} per the `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` regex; documentation of the additive 7f42 fields (source_files, deferred_test) as forward-compatible optional entries.
- OUT: any stage emitter wiring (sc-2/3/4); read/validate tooling (sc-5/6); the a03c hook (sc-7).

## Done Definitions

- intent-allocation-manifest.md exists at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ and documents every per-entry field (intent_id, owner_ticket, test_artifact.path, test_artifact.kind, deferred, lightweight, shared_infra, confidence, rationale) plus manifest-level contract_version=1 ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The contract states the validator acceptance rule verbatim: an entry is valid when intent_id matches the slug regex, owner_ticket resolves to a ticket in the epic subtree (or shared_infra is set), and test_artifact kind/path pairing holds ← Satisfies: sc-1
- intent-id-mint.sh emits a slug matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` derived from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case}, and re-running it with the same inputs returns the identical slug ← Satisfies: sc-1
- intent-id-mint.sh emits distinct slugs for two items whose first five words differ, confirming the id is not ordinal-derived ← Satisfies: sc-1
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in intent-id-mint.sh, including the stability and determinism cases ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Stability] intent_id MUST be stable across re-runs: the same DoD/item inputs mint the identical slug so a re-decomposition never re-mints a different id for the same item. This is the load-bearing invariant for all downstream merge logic.
- [Forward-compat] The contract must mandate unknown-field passthrough so the additive 7f42 fields (source_files, deferred_test) and any future consumer fields survive read/merge round-trips.
- [Shell hygiene] intent-id-mint.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation or the test gate silently skips it.
- [Scope] The 7f42 additive-field request (ticket comment) is documented here as optional schema, not implemented as behavior; downstream consumers add their own population logic.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a tooling author, I want a published intent-allocation-manifest contract with a stable intent_id schema and a mint helper, so that every pipeline stage records intent ownership in one format.
